newsitem.title: SPAIN: Retevision could be private by end-1998.
newsitem.headline: Retevision could be private by end-1998.

text.p: Spain said on Saturday that the final state stake in second telephone operator Retevision could be sold by December 1, 1998, the deadline for full liberalisation of the nation's telecommunications sector.
"This could be the date by which the state is no longer on the board," Development Minister Rafael Arias Salgado told a news conference.
Sixty percent of Retevision was awarded on Friday to the highest-bidding consortium, which is led by Spanish utility Endesa and Italian telecoms firm Stet.

The consortium has committed itself to an obligatory 10 percent capital expansion which will leave the state with a 30 percent stake in the group that will soon compete with former monopoly Telefonica de Espana.
In addition, Arias Salgado said Spain would welcome the losing consortium's participation in the Spanish market. A third telecommunications licence will be sold next year.
Opera is comprised of Banco Central Hispano, France Telecom and U.S.-based Sprint.
"I want to send them a message - we want them in the Spanish market," Arias Salgado said.
He also said the government was aiming for full liberalisation of telecommunications at that date, although technical problems might force delays in some areas.
"It's a date that one cannot take dogmatically. But there is a will for total liberalisation," Arias Salgado said.
